# Ring AllReduce: Communication Pattern for Distributed Training ## Problem: AllGather Bandwidth Standard AllGather on 8 GPUs: ``` GPU 0: has chunk A GPU 1: has chunk B GPU 2: has chunk C ... GPU 7: has chunk H AllGather: every GPU sends to every other GPU Total messages: 8 * 7 = 56 messages (each GPU sends to 7 others) Total bandwidth used: 56 messages on potentially oversubscribed network Network diameter: 3 hops (in some topologies) Latency: high due to congestion ``` --- ## Ring AllReduce Algorithm Arrange GPUs in a logical ring. Each GPU only communicates with neighbors. ``` Ring topology (logical, not physical): GPU 0 → GPU 1 → GPU 2 → ... → GPU 7 → GPU 0 AllReduce: sum all chunks, result on all GPUs (AllGather + Reduce combined) Algorithm (2 phases): Phase 1: ReduceScatter (sum chunks, scatter results) GPU 0 sends A to GPU 1 GPU 1 sends (B + A_recv) to GPU 2 GPU 2 sends (C + B_recv) to GPU 3 ... Total: N steps, each GPU sends 1 chunk Phase 2: AllGather (broadcast results back) GPU 0 sends (A + H_sum) to GPU 1 GPU 1 sends (B + A_sum) to GPU 2 ... Total: N steps Total communication: 2N steps, each step = 1 chunk sent across 1 link ``` **Ring AllReduce sequence (8 GPUs, 2 phases):** ```mermaid graph LR subgraph Phase1["Phase 1: ReduceScatter"] direction LR GPU0["GPU 0
(A)"] GPU1["GPU 1
(B)"] GPU2["GPU 2
(C)"] GPU3["GPU 3
(D)"] GPU4["GPU 4
(E)"] GPU5["GPU 5
(F)"] GPU6["GPU 6
(G)"] GPU7["GPU 7
(H)"] GPU0 -->|send A| GPU1 GPU1 -->|send B+A| GPU2 GPU2 -->|send C+B| GPU3 GPU3 -->|send D+C| GPU4 GPU4 -->|send E+D| GPU5 GPU5 -->|send F+E| GPU6 GPU6 -->|send G+F| GPU7 GPU7 -->|send H+G| GPU0 end subgraph Phase2["Phase 2: AllGather"] direction LR GPU0_2["GPU 0"] GPU1_2["GPU 1"] GPU2_2["GPU 2"] GPU3_2["GPU 3"] GPU4_2["GPU 4"] GPU5_2["GPU 5"] GPU6_2["GPU 6"] GPU7_2["GPU 7"] GPU0_2 -->|all_sum| GPU1_2 GPU1_2 -->|all_sum| GPU2_2 GPU2_2 -->|all_sum| GPU3_2 GPU3_2 -->|all_sum| GPU4_2 GPU4_2 -->|all_sum| GPU5_2 GPU5_2 -->|all_sum| GPU6_2 GPU6_2 -->|all_sum| GPU7_2 GPU7_2 -->|all_sum| GPU0_2 end Phase1 -->|every GPU has partial sum| Phase2 ``` **vs. naive AllGather:** - Naive: O(N^2) messages (congestion) - Ring: O(N) steps, linear in number of GPUs (no congestion) --- ## Bandwidth Analysis ``` Ring AllReduce with N=8 GPUs: Phase 1: GPU 0→1→2→...→7 (8 steps, pipelined) Phase 2: GPU 0→1→2→...→7 (8 steps, pipelined) Total: 16 steps Each step sends 1 chunk across 1 link (128 GB / 8 = 16 GB per chunk) If NVLink 900 GB/s: Phase 1: 16 GB / 900 GB/s = 17.8 ms per step * 8 steps = 143 ms Phase 2: 143 ms Total: 286 ms Naive AllGather (all-to-all): 56 messages, congestion → likely 500+ ms (depends on switch capacity) Ring is 50% of naive on ideal network, and much better on congested networks. ``` **Key:** Ring is bandwidth-optimal for AllReduce. Each network link carries exactly one chunk, no redundancy. --- ## Latency vs Bandwidth Trade-off Ring AllReduce has high latency (sequential steps) but high bandwidth efficiency. ``` Latency: 2N network hops (serial dependencies) Bandwidth: efficient, no congestion vs. Tree AllReduce: Latency: O(log N) hops (much lower) Bandwidth: requires 2x bandwidth on top links (congestion) Choice: Small N (< 16 GPUs): Tree AllReduce (latency-bound) Large N (32+ GPUs): Ring AllReduce (bandwidth-bound) ``` --- ## Q&A **Recall 1:** How does ring AllReduce reduce congestion vs naive AllGather? *Answer:* Ring arranges GPUs in a logical ring and sends each chunk along the ring once per phase. Each network link carries exactly one chunk (no redundancy). Naive AllGather sends each chunk to every other GPU (O(N^2) messages), causing congestion on shared links. **Numeric 1:** 16 GPUs, chunk size 64 GB, NVLink 900 GB/s. Ring AllReduce time? *Working:* Phase 1: 16 steps * 64 GB / 900 GB/s ≈ 16 * 71 ms ≈ 1136 ms. Hmm, that's high. Actually, pipelining helps: first chunk is 71 ms, subsequent chunks overlap. So ~71 ms total for phase 1 if pipelined. Actually, let me recalculate: in ring allreduce, each GPU sends one chunk per step. With pipelining, after the first chunk is sent by GPU 0, GPU 1 can send immediately (they send in parallel on different links). So phase 1 is 64 GB / 900 GB/s ≈ 71 ms (not 16x longer). Total: 2 phases = 142 ms. Much better than 1136 ms. **Probe 1:** You have 32 GPUs across 2 machines (16 per machine). Inter-machine link is 50 GB/s (slow), intra-machine NVLink is 900 GB/s. Ring AllReduce will be bottlenecked by inter-machine link. How do you optimize? *Expected:* Use hierarchical AllReduce: Ring AllReduce within each machine (fast), then Tree AllReduce across machines (few hops). Or separate TP (intra-machine) from DP (inter-machine).
